<description>
The secp256k1 subtree is built without our hardening flags. They are on `core_interface`, and `cmake/secp256k1.cmake` passes the subtree only the sanitizer and `APPEND_*` flags, so unless the compiler enables them by default its objects miss FORTIFY, the stack protector, stack clash protection and control flow protection. On aarch64 Ubuntu 26.04 with GCC 15 this also costs the whole binary its control flow property: master's `bitcoind` has no `AArch64 feature` note, and the three secp256k1 objects are the only ones in the build tree without it.

This PR moves the flags back to a `hardening_interface` library, which `core_interface` links; the `CMakeLists.txt` change is a revert of 77e553ab6a plus one comment. `cmake/secp256k1.cmake` then passes them to the subtree the same way as `sanitize_interface`. With it, the same build shows `AArch64 feature: BTI, PAC, GCS` on `bitcoind`. It does not fix #30677 on its own: the depends libraries are still built without `-fcf-protection`, which #30685 tried to change.
</description>

<commits>
09509dde1d build: pass hardening flags to secp256k1

The hardening flags are added to core_interface, which the secp256k1
subtree does not use: cmake/secp256k1.cmake passes it only the
sanitizer and APPEND_* flags. Its objects are therefore built without
_FORTIFY_SOURCE, -fstack-protector-all, -fstack-clash-protection,
-fcf-protection and -mbranch-protection, unless the compiler enables
them by default.

This also drops the control flow property from the binaries. The
linker marks an executable as BTI/PAC (aarch64) or IBT/SHSTK (x86_64)
enabled only when every object it links has the property. On aarch64
Ubuntu 26.04 with GCC 15, bitcoind built from master has no AArch64
feature property, and the secp256k1 objects are the only objects in
the build tree without it.

Move the hardening flags to a hardening_interface library, which
core_interface links, and pass its compile and link options to the
subtree in the same way as sanitize_interface. This brings back the
hardening_interface that was folded into core_interface in 77e553ab6a,
now that the flags have a second user.
</commits>
